title: The Slab Allocator: An Object-Caching Kernel Memory Allocator
why_anghel: Canonical size-class object caching; mental model for engine pools and multipools.
abstract_or_blurb: Bonwick's slab allocator caches initialized objects by size class, reducing fragmentation and constructor cost in kernel heaps.

title: Magazines and Vmem: Extending the Slab Allocator to Many CPUs and Arbitrary Resources
why_anghel: Per-CPU magazines + vmem layer: the multipool / resource-arena pattern games rediscover constantly.
abstract_or_blurb: Extends slabs with per-CPU magazines and a general virtual memory resource allocator (vmem) for scalable multiprocessor allocation.

title: Hoard: A Scalable Memory Allocator for Multithreaded Applications
why_anghel: Avoids heap blowup under threads; cautionary + design notes for Anoptic's mimalloc world.
abstract_or_blurb: Hoard provides scalable concurrent allocation with per-processor heaps while bounding allocator-induced fragmentation.

title: A Scalable Concurrent malloc(3) Implementation for FreeBSD (jemalloc)
why_anghel: Arena-of-arenas design; still the mental model for many runtime heaps.
abstract_or_blurb: jemalloc introduces multiple arenas and careful size-class layout for scalable concurrent malloc on FreeBSD and beyond.

title: snmalloc: A Message Passing Allocator
why_anghel: Message-passing remote frees; relevant to wait-free-ish engine heaps.
abstract_or_blurb: snmalloc uses message passing for cross-thread deallocation and a modern size-class design.

title: SuperMalloc: A Super Fast Multithreaded malloc for 64-bit Machines
why_anghel: Aggressive 64-bit multithreaded malloc engineering notes.
abstract_or_blurb: SuperMalloc optimizes large-address-space multithreaded allocation with careful page and size-class strategies.

title: Mesh: Compacting Memory Management for C/C++ Applications
why_anghel: Randomized compaction without relocating pointers via page aliasing — fragmentation countermeasure.
abstract_or_blurb: Mesh compactifies heaps by mapping multiple virtual pages to one physical page when contents are compatible.

title: DieHard: Probabilistic Memory Safety for Unsafe Languages
why_anghel: Allocator as fault isolation; useful foil for deterministic game heaps.
abstract_or_blurb: DieHard uses randomization and replication in the allocator to probabilistically tolerate memory errors.

title: Local Memory Allocators in Large-Scale C++ (Lakos allocator model)
why_anghel: Polymorphic local allocators, multipool, and allocator-aware interfaces — the Lakos discipline for engine subsystems.
abstract_or_blurb: Lakos argues for local (scoped) allocators and multipool strategies so allocation policy is a first-class combinatorial property of C++ components.

title: Allocator-Aware (AA) Software (Lakos et al.)
why_anghel: Modern Lakos AA vocabulary for propagating allocators through types — maps to arena/region wiring in Anoptic.
abstract_or_blurb: Presents allocator-aware software design: propagating memory suppliers through vocabulary types without hidden global new.

title: Dynamic Storage Allocation: A Survey and Critical Review
why_anghel: Still the best map of freelists, buddy, segregated fits, fragmentation taxonomy.
abstract_or_blurb: Surveys decades of dynamic storage allocation mechanisms and fragmentation behavior with a critical taxonomy.

title: An Efficient Memory Allocator for Network Processors and Multiprocessors (TLSF)
why_anghel: O(1) real-time allocator — relevant when sim ticks have hard budgets.
abstract_or_blurb: TLSF (Two-Level Segregated Fit) provides bounded-time malloc/free suitable for real-time systems.

title: Data-Oriented Design and C++
why_anghel: The sermon Anoptic already lives by: throughput, SoA, solve for data.
abstract_or_blurb: Acton presents data-oriented design as organizing code around data transformation and cache reality rather than object hierarchies.

title: Entity Systems are the future of MMOG development (T-Machine series)
why_anghel: Early public ECS articulation that shaped indie/engine discourse.
abstract_or_blurb: Argues for entities as IDs with components in tables, systems as transforms — especially for large online worlds.

title: A Journey into Entity Component Systems
why_anghel: Clear node/family formulation of ECS queries.
abstract_or_blurb: Explains ECS via Ash: entities, components, and systems matched through families/nodes.

title: Evolve Your Hierarchy
why_anghel: Component composition over deep inheritance — bridge from OOP games to ECS.
abstract_or_blurb: Advocates decomposing game object hierarchies into component aggregates to regain flexibility and performance.

title: Unity ECS / DOTS architecture overview (Entities package docs)
why_anghel: Industrial archetype chunk ECS at scale; foil/benchmark for Anoptic layouts.
abstract_or_blurb: Unity Entities stores components in archetype chunks processed by Burst-friendly systems.

title: Flecs: A Fast Entity Component System for C99
why_anghel: Query language + relationships in ECS — closest OSS cousin to ano-shaped thinking.
abstract_or_blurb: Flecs provides a high-performance ECS with expressive queries, relationships, and hierarchies in C99.

title: EnTT: Gaming meets modern C++
why_anghel: Sparse-set ECS design notes widely copied in C++ engines.
abstract_or_blurb: Series explaining EnTT's sparse set component pools and view/group iteration model.

title: Our Machinery Component System / data-oriented engine notes
why_anghel: Practitioner ECS+rendering integration notes from Bitsquid lineage.
abstract_or_blurb: Discusses practical ECS design choices interacting with rendering and engine modules.

title: Bitsquid Data-Driven / Entity system posts
why_anghel: Stingray/Bitsquid entity system: data-driven, ID-based, production-proven.
abstract_or_blurb: Describes building a data-oriented entity system with arrays of components and late-bound references.

title: Overwatch Gameplay Architecture and Netcode (ECS-flavored)
why_anghel: ECS-ish gameplay + networking discipline at shipped scale.
abstract_or_blurb: GDC talk on Overwatch gameplay architecture, component-oriented simulation, and netcode implications.

title: Using Relational Databases for Entity-Component Systems
why_anghel: Relational view of components-as-tables — bridge toward ano query DNA without LLM noise.
abstract_or_blurb: Frames ECS as relational tables where systems are queries/joins over component relations.

title: Archetypal ECS storage and iteration (chunked archetypes pattern)
why_anghel: Archetype chunk storage is the default high-perf ECS layout to compare against Anoptic SoA.
abstract_or_blurb: Archetypal ECS stores entities sharing a component signature in contiguous chunks for SIMD-friendly system iteration.
